posts.text:
Louisiana, let’s finish strong! 🔥 Today is the LAST DAY to vote early. Yes, you can wait until Election Day on November 3rd, but you never know what may come up. Polls are open until 6:00 PM! 

Let’s turn out the vote! #VoteEarlyLouisiana https://t.co/lmB4NHwsIe
Tomorrow is the last day to vote early, Louisiana. Get up, get out and VOTE! #YourVoteIsYourVoice #VoteEarly https://t.co/4JcwzUPn9L
Regardless of intent, a remark such as this puts the safety and security of millions of Americans at risk and should not be taken lightly! https://t.co/UJ3P3ju6GW

Some visits just mean a little more. 💛💙

Today, Congress to the Classroom brought me back to my beloved alma mater, Southern University and A&M College, for a special opportunity to engage with some of our state’s brightest young minds!

We took a deep dive into the branches of government, the legislative process, and the importance of civic engagement. But the highlight of today’s visit was hearing from the students themselves. I was so proud of their genuine interest in how they can become more engaged.

I reminded them that their ability to make a difference starts at the ballot box, and when young people across America become informed, engaged, and involved, they truly hold the power to drive meaningful change.

Yesterday at the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation’s 55th Annual Legislative Conference, I had the opportunity to lead an important conversation on Louisiana v. Callais and the future of voting rights in America.

I was joined by Rep. Jonathan Jackson, Tara Murray, Janai Nelson, and Rep. Shomari Figures for a timely discussion on the Voting Rights Act, fair representation, and what the Callais case could mean for equal access to the ballot.

At a pivotal moment for voting rights, conversations like these are critical as we continue working to protect the right of every American to have their voice heard and their vote represented.

On this 25th anniversary of September 11, we honor the lives lost and the countless families forever changed.

Time moves forward, but we will never forget. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/tqFScsn4NP

Voting rights are on the line. Join me and leading voices in the fight for voting rights at #ALC55 for a timely conversation on Louisiana v. Callais, the Voting Rights Act, and what’s at stake for fair representation. https://t.co/Lau8f3yRUG

The other day, I joined Jim Engster with Talk Louisiana to discuss the state of our politics and what’s at stake heading into November.

The American people are frustrated, and they’re looking for relief.

I believe voters are going to head to the polls this November and vote their conscience. They want better government, stronger leadership, and a Congress that will stand up for them.

I’m optimistic about Democrats’ chances of taking back the House and the Senate, but we cannot take anything for granted. We have to organize, show up, and make sure every eligible voter gets to the polls.

The work starts now.

NATCHITOCHES, LA — Congressman Cleo Fields (LA-06) today announced that Northwestern State University has been awarded $1.8 million in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to support the university's Innovation Park Equipment Expansion (IPEX) Project. The funding request was submitted in collaboration with U.S. Senators Bill Cassidy and John Kennedy.
 
The award will allow the university to purchase cutting-edge equipment for Innovation Park, including an AI supercomputer, laser cutters, and advanced 3D printers.
 
Read the full release here: https://t.co/rNz29wWaN7

This Friday, I’m heading back into the classroom! 📚

Congress to the Classroom continues in West Baton Rouge Parish on August 28. I’m looking forward to visiting with students, answering their questions, and talking with them about public service and the work we do in Congress.

📍 Port Allen Elementary — 8:40 AM
📍 Cohn Intermediate — 9:30 AM
📍 Brusly Middle School — 10:25 AM

See you Friday!

After much deliberation, I have decided not to seek re-election to Congress, and will instead be running to fill the unexpired term for the State Senate in the 14th District. 

Read my full statement here, and stay tuned for more information this Friday. https://t.co/wiIbZY97Gb

Some losses are hard to put into words. Larry Selders was a dear friend of mine and an amazing man, and Louisiana will not be the same without him. My thoughts, prayers, and condolences are with Kendra, LJ, Luke, and everyone who loved him. 

Rest well, my friend.

To read my full statement, visit https://t.co/PFo9h2jHRm.

Heartbroken by the passing of Senator Larry Selders. He was a great man who gave everything to the people of Louisiana, and this loss will be felt deeply across our state. Praying for his wife, his sons, and all who loved him. Rest in peace, my friend.

Thank you, Natchitoches, for joining me at last week’s town hall. The change we want to see starts with us being present and engaging with the issues that affect our Louisiana communities. Keep on showing up and keep on speaking out. #LA06 https://t.co/KeTc5fjdmn

This Memorial Day, we honor our fallen heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our nation. 

We will forever remember their courage, honor their legacy, and keep their loved ones in our prayers. https://t.co/pLcWuLVtpk

Our support for Black athletes cannot begin and end with entertainment. I went to Congress to fight for them on and off the field — and that’s exactly what I did today alongside the CBC and NAACP.

For my full statement, visit https://t.co/kKQSDDbmtn. 

#LA06 #CleoFields #CBC #NAACP #VotingRights

This past weekend, I had the incredible opportunity to speak at the Rainbow PUSH Saturday Morning Forum about recent developments to the Voting Rights Act and how best to stay engaged with our nation’s civic process.

It’s important that everyone stays engaged in the civic process. Change doesn’t happen on its own — it happens when people show up, speak out, and vote.

Yesterday I had the pleasure of sitting down with my long time friend @donlemonofficial and @nolathaprogressive to discuss how people nationwide can stay engaged and stay involved in our country’s civic process. 

Now more than ever, it’s important that everyone knows their power. Whether it’s voting, volunteering, or simply having conversations like this one — change starts with us.

#LA06 #CleoFields #DonLemon #VotingRights

The demographics of this state demand fair representation. The history of this state demands it. And the people of Louisiana — ALL of the people — deserve nothing less. 

#LA06 #VotingRights #CleoFields #LouisianaStrong https://t.co/ieB7S1XySz

Last night I joined @thelauracoates on CNN to break down the Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision — and what the Governor’s executive order suspending House primaries actually means for Louisiana voters.

Absentee ballots have been cast. Early voting was about to start. And now those votes won’t count. Nothing in the Court’s ruling required this. This was a choice — one that disenfranchises real voters for political gain. 

Let the election proceed as planned. Every Louisianan deserves to have their vote counted.

I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: this issue is bigger than District 6. This is about black voters throughout the Southern part of our country having the tools to let their voices be heard. 

The federal government should be doing everything in its power to provide fair representation to all Americans. That’s why Congress needs to pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act as soon as possible. 

#VotingRights #VotingRightsAct #CongressionalBlackCaucus

The Governor's Executive Order suspending the House primaries is the wrong move. Louisianans have already cast absentee ballots, early voting was set to begin this weekend, and now those votes won't count. That is unacceptable. Legal experts have made clear that nothing in the Supreme Court's ruling requires us to halt these elections — that is a choice the Governor is making. 

Rather than disenfranchising voters mid-election to redraw maps for political gain, we should let this election proceed as planned under the existing districts and address any redistricting in the proper cycle. The fundamental right of every Louisianan to have their vote counted must not be sacrificed for a rushed political agenda.

Yesterday, I spoke with @stephenasmith on his Straight Shooter with Stephen A show to talk about the Supreme Court decision on Louisiana v. Callais and how this will impact District 6 and the nation. 

It’s important for voters to know that representation is on the line and this is not the time to lose hope. It’s time to show up, stay engaged, and vote in record numbers in November.

#LA06 #LouisianaStrong #StraightShooterWithStephenA #StephenASmith #VotingRights #VotingRightsAct

conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
